blocks.text: The conflict between Ahab and Micaiah brings First Kings’ larger movement into focus: the book has moved from disputed succession through Solomon’s wisdom, temple, and failure, into divided kingdoms and prophetic confrontation under Ahab. This chapter therefore closes Ahab’s story with a direct clash between royal plans and prophetic speech.

An inscription known as the Kurkh Monolith names Ahab in a coalition at Qarqar, an event not narrated in First Kings. It independently places an Israelite king in ninth-century regional politics, though it does not establish every detail or theological claim made in the book.
